chapter_mission: Torin leaves. Ben tries to stop him, Sera silently realizes force would make things worse, and the group chooses the hardest form of restraint: letting him walk because they will not repeat the old pattern.
chapter_turn: Ben moves from "I have to stop him" to "We find another way. Together." The decision is morally right, tactically necessary, and devastating precisely because no one can hide inside a speech.

scene_plan.purpose: Torin makes his decision plain and Ben cannot talk him out of it. Sera catches the shape of the danger in silence and passes it to Ben with a look.
The group watches Torin leave and realizes that stopping him by force would repeat the crime they are trying to escape. Each person's silence should feel different.
Ben names the only path left to them: not mastery, but another way together. The plan is still incomplete, but the pattern has changed.

relationship_turns.to: departed — Torin walks. Sera does not move to stop him and does not look away. She has also just read, silently, the counter-preparation he built because he anticipated her. The dynamic ends; the grief begins. Per B2, her Force-lock read is the diagnostic instrument for Torin's counter-preparation — a specific expression of her Ch 20-era lie_cracking phase

relationship_turns.from: named once (Ch 18) — Ben has carried the parallel privately since
relationship_turns.to: broken — Ben publicly refuses to repeat it. Jacen was the ghost. Breaking the pattern is the answer. Per R13, the Jacen name does NOT land again here; the refusal is enacted through the decision, not named. Per B2, the refusal is also tactically correct, which strengthens rather than weakens the Jacen-parallel payoff

relationship_turns.from: conditional trust ('Tell me where to stand, Skywalker') from Ch 14; genuine request from Ch 19
relationship_turns.to: earned trust — Sera has seen Ben refuse the old pattern; she will follow him on his terms now, not because he is the senior officer but because he proved incompatible with Gavran. Her silent Force-lock read is also the first time her expertise has directly shaped a book-level decision

tactical peer — Desh's readings are now load-bearing data in Ben's decision-making. He is not Ben's plus-one; he is the operational second whose numbers combine with Sera's read to produce the room's silent consensus
witnessing commitment — Kael watches the group not seal Torin. He sees what it costs them. His lie_cracking phase advances; H22 is now in reach

exit_vector: Camp silent on the ridge. Torin a diminishing figure in the valley below. Ben lowers the datapad, looks at Sera, Kael, Desh. 'We find another way. Together.' The Lie is not healed — but for the first time, it is no longer the loudest voice in the room. Three reasons for letting Torin walk; one of them spoken. The decision the book has been building toward since Ch 1 is made.
notes: The chapter works if the room carries three kinds of knowledge without overexplaining any of them: grief, danger, and refusal. Torin should remain warm and certain, not villainous. Sera's read belongs in a glance, a hand, a change in posture. Desh's contribution should come through the practical pressure he has been tracking, not through a lecture. Let the silence do most of the chapter's work; Sera gets one line, Ben gets one line, and the rest should live in what each person cannot make themselves do.
